'''Eugene Michael Chudnovsky''' (born 12 December 1948) is a Distinguished Professor of Physics at [[Lehman College]]<ref name="LehmanFaculty">Lehman College, Chudnovsky in the list of Faculty.</ref><ref name="CunyProfile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cuny.edu/about/people/faculty/bios.html?profName=eugenemchudnovsky&profile=0 |title=Chudnovsky's profile of a Distinguished Professor of CUNY |access-date=2012-02-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825154649/http://www.cuny.edu/about/people/faculty/bios.html?profName=eugenemchudnovsky&profile=0 |archive-date=2012-08-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a member of the doctoral faculty at the [[Graduate Center of the City University of New York]]. Chudnovsky is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS), elected 1993<ref name="APSFellow1993">[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=C&year=1993&unit_id=&institution= Chudnovsky - APS Fellow]</ref> for "seminal contributions to random ferromagnetism, macroscopic quantum tunneling, and hexatic order in high Tc materials". He is mostly known for his work on quantum tunneling of magnetization.<ref name="MQT">[http://www.nature.com/milestones/milespin/full/milespin22.html Tunneling of magnetization]</ref> Chudnovsky explained magnetic avalanches experimentally observed in [[Single-molecule magnet|molecular magnets]] as [[deflagration]].<ref name="MagneticBurning">[http://www.physorg.com/news5967.html "Magnetic flames"]</ref>

Chudnovsky received his undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral education at [[University of Kharkiv|Kharkiv University]] in Ukraine, in the school of theoretical physics founded by [[Lev Landau]] and his students. The denial by the USSR of an exit visa to Chudnovsky in 1979 led to his unemployment for eight years, during which he continued independent research in theoretical physics and participated in the unofficial [[Refusenik]] Science Seminar in Moscow.<ref name="AlpertBook">[https://www.amazon.com/Making-Waves-Stories-My-Life/dp/0300078218 Making Waves: Stories from My Life by Yakov Alpert]</ref> He was frequently harassed and interrogated by the [[KGB]].

In 1987 Chudnovsky was allowed to emigrate and joined the faculty of the physics department of [[Tufts University]] in Boston. The following year he moved to the [[City University of New York]] (CUNY). He has held visiting positions at research centers in the US, Asia, and Europe—most notably at the [[University of Barcelona]] - Spain, where he co-organizes Annual International Workshop on Magnetism and Superconductivity.<ref name="ComaRugaConference">[http://www.ub.edu/gmag/comaruga/ Coma-Ruga Conference on Magnetism and Superconductivity]</ref>

Chudnovsky has been active in the field of human rights. He has served as chair of the APS Committee on International Freedom of Scientists, Member-at-Large<ref name="Member-at-Large-Election">[https://www.aps.org/units/fip/newsletters/201309/forum.cfm APS Committee on International Freedom of Scientists, Chudnovsky's Member-at-large candidacy]</ref><ref name="Chudnovsky - Member-at-Large Lehman">{{Cite web |url=http://www.lehman.edu/lehmantoday/2011_03/t_chudnovsky.html |title=Chudnovsky - Member-at-large, from Lehman College news |access-date=2012-02-22 |archive-date=2011-12-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111229215321/http://www.lehman.edu/lehmantoday/2011_03/t_chudnovsky.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>  of the [http://www.aps.org/units/fip/ Forum on International Physics], Chair of the Committee on Human Rights of Scientists of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]], and co-chair of the [[Committee of Concerned Scientists]]. In 1990s he directed Program for Refugee Scientists that resettled over one hundred refugee scientists in the United States.

Chudnovsky is a recipient of the 2024 [[Andrei Sakharov Prize (APS)]]<ref name="SakharovPrize">[https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/prize/andrei-sakharov Andrei Sakharov Prize (APS) - the list of awardees]</ref> of the American Physical Society, awarded to him “for decades of leadership of prominent campaigns on behalf of oppressed scientists, including chairmanship of the APS and New York Academy of Sciences human rights committees and co-chairing of the Committee of Concerned Scientists.”

;Selected papers

:E. M. Chudnovsky, W. M. Saslow, and R. A. Serota, [http://prb.aps.org/abstract/PRB/v33/i1/p251_1 "Ordering in ferromagnets with random anisotropy"], ''Physical Review'' B 33, 251 (1986).

: E. M. Chudnovsky and L. Gunther, [http://prl.aps.org/abstract/PRL/v60/i8/p661_1 "Quantum tunneling of magnetization in small ferromagnetic particles"], ''Physical Review Letters'' 60, 661 (1988)].

: E. M. Chudnovsky, [http://prb.aps.org/abstract/PRB/v40/i16/p11355_1 "Hexatic vortex glass in disordered superconductors"], ''Physical Review'' B 40, 11355 (1989)].

: E. M. Chudnovsky, [http://pra.aps.org/abstract/PRA/v46/i12/p8011_1 "Phase transitions in the problem of the decay of a metastable state"], ''Physical Review'' A 46, 8011 (1992)].

: E. M. Chudnovsky, [http://prl.aps.org/abstract/PRL/v92/i12/e120405 "Universal decoherence in solids"], ''Physical Review Letters'' 92, 120405 (2004)].

:E. M. Chudnovsky, J. Tejada, and E. Punset (in Spanish): [https://www.amazon.com/El-Templo-Ciencia-Cientificos-Creencias/dp/8423340163/ref=sr_1_1?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1329940068&sr=1-1 "El Templo de la Ciencia"], Destino – Spain, 2008].
